title: Psychology Field Interest Explorer
disclaimer: This educational activity reflects the preferences you select today. It is not a diagnosis, validated psychological test, MBTI assessment, admissions recommendation, or career prediction.
methodology: For each field, your 1–5 responses are converted to a 0–4 preference value, multiplied by the visible field weights, and scaled independently from 0 to 100. Field percentages do not need to add up to 100.

questions.prompt: Designing a small experiment to learn why people remember some information better than other information.
Exploring how groups, friendships, and the desire to belong can influence a person's choices.
Learning how children and teenagers change in the ways they think, feel, and relate to others.
Studying how language, culture, and identity shape the way people understand the world.
Investigating what happens in the brain while someone learns, focuses, or makes a choice.
Understanding why people respond differently to the same event without reducing them to a personality label.
Exploring how stress, sleep, habits, and daily environments relate to wellbeing.
Comparing how people judge risk, weigh options, and make decisions under uncertainty.
Evaluating evidence about programs intended to support mental health and community wellbeing.
Using interviews, observations, or surveys to understand emotion and relationships in everyday life.
